title: BFS Computing Unweighted Shortest Edge Distances

guide.problem: Find reachable vertices and shortest unweighted routes.
guide.design: Breadth-first search uses arrival layers; depth-first search explores a branch. DFS is not a shortest-edge-path substitute.
guide.invariant: BFS marks a vertex when enqueued so it enters the queue once.
guide.failure: Marking only on removal adds duplicate work. Following one DFS branch does not establish the shortest route.
guide.maintenance: Test disconnected graphs, self-loops, cycles, and the returned path witness.
guide.scope: This panel connects this listing to its chapter’s problem. Short demonstrations illustrate one part; the chapter’s complete implementation and invariant labs test the broader contract.

experiment: Predict one boundary or tie case, then change this listing and trace the affected state. With 0->1,0->2,2->3, BFS distances from 0 are 0,1,1,2.
